question.text: What is the process called when previously issued paper share certificates are converted into electronic form?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, dematerialisation is the conversion of previously issued share certificates (and other physical securities) into electronic form. The Trap: Rematerialisation is the opposite process, converting electronic holdings back to physical certificates. Securitisation is the process of pooling financial assets into tradable securities. Capitalisation refers to converting reserves into share capital. Note: Both source pages (one defining the conversion of previously issued share certificates into electronic form and the other defining conversion of physical securities to electronic form) support the same term: dematerialisation.
